name: Prothrombin Time
overview: Prothrombin Time is a health topic that clinicians and patients frequently discuss during care planning in India and worldwide. Key considerations include the prothrombin time (pt) – along with its derived measures of prothrombin ratio (pr) and international normalized ratio (inr) – is an assay for evaluating the extrinsic pathway and common pathway of coagulation; this blood test is also called protime inr and pt/inr; they are used to determine the clotting tendency of blood, in conditions such as the measure of warfarin dosage, liver damage (cirrhosis), and vitamin k status. This summary is educational and should be paired with professional medical evaluation.

Health professionals note that this blood test is also called protime INR and PT/INR.
In routine practice, they are used to determine the clotting tendency of blood, in conditions such as the measure of warfarin dosage, liver damage (cirrhosis), and vitamin K status.
In routine practice, pT measures the following coagulation factors: I (fibrinogen), II (prothrombin), V (proaccelerin), VII (proconvertin), and X.
